legend: Predominantly intracanalicular pattern. Expansion of the stroma compresses the ductal element to form slit-like spaces. Note the rounded border.
Pericanalicular pattern, with stromal growth around patent ducts.
An FNA specimen showing fibroadenoma with benign branched epithelial fragments in small sheets. A stromal fragment is also seen.
Aspirate showing broad branching of the epithelium, resembling a staghorn, with bland-looking epithelial cells. The background shows naked bipolar nuclei.
The macroscopic appearance of a fibroadenoma reveals a circumscribed boundary with distinct separation from the adjacent adipose tissue. The cut surface shows whitish whorled fibrous tissue.
Core biopsy shows tissue cores with a nodular proliferation of both the epithelial and stromal components.

diagnosis: Invasive breast carcinoma extending into fibroadenoma
legend: Invasive carcinoma cells extend into the fibrotic stroma of a fibroadenoma.
An excised fibroadenoma showing a smooth, lobulated yellow surface. The fibroadenoma is shelled out, with little adherent adjacent tissue.

legend: Intracanalicular pattern: the lesion shows circumscribed margins and an intracanalicular pattern of growth.
Circumscribed margins and mildly increased stromal cellularity but with no fronds or stromal atypia.

diagnosis: Fibroadenoma involved by low-grade ductal carcinoma in situ
legend: The lesion shows ducts expanded by a monotonous population of ductal cells with small nuclei and exhibiting rigid cribriform spaces consistent with low-grade ductal carcinoma in situ.
The lesion shows hypocellular hyalinized stroma
Gross appearance of a circumscribed and slightly lobulated fibroadenoma with a whitish whorled cut surface.
The lesion is generally circumscribed with lobulated contours, with a partly irregular interface with adjacent fat along its periphery.
Gross appearance of a fibroadenoma that shows a mild increase in stromal cellularity on microscopy. The cut surface is glistening and greyish beige with focal haemorrhages due to its fresh state.
Mild increase in stromal cellularity.
Juvenile fibroadenoma: the lesion shows a pericanalicular growth pattern comprising scattered ducts with mild usual ductal hyperplasia within a mildly cellular stroma.
Complex fibroadenoma: the lesion shows sclerosing adenosis, cysts, and calcifications within the lesion; papillary apocrine metaplasia is not present.
Myxoid fibroadenoma: the lesion shows a myxoid stroma containing a few chronic inflammatory cells.
Core biopsy shows a fibroadenoma with invasive lobular carcinoma and lobular carcinoma in situ.
A higher-power view of the lesion shown in Fig. <<#51444>>.
While the majority of fibroadenomas show circumscribed contours, some typical fibroadenomas may display an irregular border.
Hyalinised fibroadenoma with sclerosing adenosis and occasional calcifications.

legend: Encapsulated fibroadenoma with a predominantly intracanalicular growth pattern.
Cellular fibroadenoma shows mild increase in stromal cellularity with variable approximation of stromal nuclei that sometimes touch one another. No fronded architecture is seen.

Vacuum assisted breast biopsy shows a fibroadenoma with pericanalicular and intracanalicular growth patterns in mildly oedematous to focally inflamed stroma. The epithelial component shows mild to moderate usual ductal hyperplasia. 
The fibroadenoma shows an irregular boundary with surrounding adipose tissue in some cores. 
No histological features of a phyllodes tumour are present such as stromal hypercellularity, atypia, obvious mitoses, expansile stromal fronds.
Fibrocystic changes and pseudoangiomatous stromal hyperplasia are noted in the adjacent breast.
Blood clots are included.
(H&E)

diagnosis: Fibroadenoma with adipocytic and focal chondroid metaplasia
legend: Benign neoplasm with components of fibroadenoma, mature adipose tissue and a chondroid island. The differential diagnoses are between a fibroadenoma with adipose and chondroid metaplasia, versus a hamartoma. The former diagnosis is favoured as there is a well-formed fibroadenoma, whereas the hamartoma generally has a ‘breast within a breast’ appearance, with mostly normal but disorganised breast tissue occurring within a circumscribed lesion.

Vacuum assisted breast biopsy from a lactating female shows a fibroadenoma with a predominantly pericanalicular growth pattern. The epithelial component shows secretory changes in the form of closely packed tubules lined by epithelial cells having pale to pink, vacuolated cytoplasm with occasional apical blebs.
A fibroadenoma with predominantly pericanalicular pattern and a prominent myxoid stroma. Adjacent breast shows mild fibrocystic changes and adenosis.
